subject: Veridian: end-to-end tail commitments and live-demo window
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Li <sophia@veridian.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: latency targets, streaming concurrency, next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion and very helpful signals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key acceptance targets you emphasized
- P95 end-to-end (API entry -> token emitted): target <= 120 ms for single-token requests under steady-state traffic.
- P99 end-to-end: target <= 420 ms (we heard +/- 50 ms tolerance during burst testing).
- Streaming: need headroom for 100 concurrent streaming sessions with an average churn of 20 req/min per session.
- Throughput: baseline 300 req/s with burst capacity to 800 req/s for 2-minute windows.

Open clarifications we promised to follow up on
1) Measurement envelope: you wanted the p95/p99 numbers measured from the client HTTP request start -> last token chunk received, inclusive of network egress time. We'll mirror your harness.
2) Burst profile: you sent an example traffic profile (Carlos) — please confirm the 90s spike shape.
3) Streaming buffer behavior: confirm desired max in-flight tokens per session (we asked if 64 tokens is acceptable).

Attachments we shared
- redwood_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (latency projections across instance types + quantization profiles)
- veridian_traffic_profile_v2.json (please confirm this is the traffic shape you used today)

Proposed next steps
- Internal sizing + demo plan: Redwood technical demo with live traffic replay (we propose Tue Feb 28 or Wed Feb 29, 10:00–11:00 PT). Will demonstrate hosted API under your profile and run side-by-side with the incumbent.
- Required from Veridian: a sanitized 30-minute traffic log (or use the attached profile) and a test API key for sandboxed replay.
- Success criteria for demo: p95 within 120 ms and p99 under 420 ms for 95% of runs; streaming concurrency maintained without buffer underflow for 90% of sessions.

If that aligns, we'll lock a demo slot and Ben will send the runbook + temporary demo credentials.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)
Attachment: veridian_traffic_profile_v2.json (JSON, 14KB)

From: Sophia Li <sophia@veridian.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency targets, streaming concurrency, next steps

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Measurement: yes, please measure client-side as you described (request start -> last chunk received). That aligns with our SLOs.
- Burst profile: attached profile is what we used; the 90s spike is correct but note it can hit 1k req/s in extreme weekends. For the demo, the attached veridian_traffic_profile_v2.json should be the canonical input.
- Streaming tokens: 64 tokens max per update is fine; most sessions average 28 tokens.

Two asks before we lock a demo
1) Can you include a quick comparison of expected token-cost delta between hosted (your configured batch/cache settings) vs our current provider (we care about unit economics at scale)?
2) For the live replay, we need a non-prod endpoint that is isolated from telemetry going into our production analytics.

We can do Tue Feb 28 10am PT. Will confirm by EOD.

Sincerely,
Sophia Li
VP Product
Veridian

--

Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 13:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: latency targets, streaming concurrency, next steps

Sophia — great, glad we're aligned on measurement and token caps. Quick technical clarifications and what we'll run in the demo: 

What Redwood will exercise in the demo
- Hosted API (redwood-hosted-prod-sandbox) with two model variants: quantized 4-bit and full-fp16 baseline. We'll show p95/p99 per-variant.
- KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes (we'll show runs with cache warm and cold).
- Continuous batching: we'll tune the batching window to respect 120ms p95 for single-token flows.
- Streaming session concurrency: we'll spin up 150 concurrent streams (above your ask) to demonstrate headroom.

Metrics we'll produce live
- p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end), tail percentiles broken by model variant and by streaming vs non-streaming paths.
- Token cost estimate per 1M requests across the two configurations (will present a simple delta table during demo).

Security / isolation
- We'll provision a temporary tenant in our hosted sandbox that never writes to Veridian production analytics and will rotate credentials after the demo.

Requested from Veridian
- A sanitized 30-minute sample (or confirmation that the attached veridian_traffic_profile_v2.json is canonical).
- Which model family you're currently using at the incumbent (helps us pick nearest baseline).

I'll prepare a 1-page runbook and a short script so your infra team can watch the replay. If Tue Feb 28 10:00 PT works, I'll send calendar invites + runbook by tomorrow morning.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
